description: How organisations describe, govern and connect their business, application, data and technology layers, and how separate systems are integrated through APIs, messaging and services. Students model architectures, build and test integrations, and plan the modernisation of a legacy estate.
modelledOn: The Open Group, TOGAF Standard (architecture development method)
Hohpe and Woolf, Enterprise Integration Patterns
outcomes: Describe an organisation using business, application, data and technology layers and capture them in an architecture modelling notation.
Analyse an application portfolio and recommend which systems to keep, integrate, replace or retire.
Design and test integrations using REST APIs, message queues and publish-subscribe, choosing patterns for a stated reliability need.
Compare monolithic, service-oriented and microservice designs and handle distributed data consistency with sagas and idempotency.
Produce a gap analysis, transition architecture and roadmap, and defend it before an architecture review board.

units.title: Enterprise architecture frameworks and layers
topics: Why enterprise architecture: strategy alignment, business capabilities and value streams
Frameworks: the TOGAF architecture development method, Zachman and government architecture frameworks; tailoring a framework
Architecture layers: business, application, data and technology
Modelling with ArchiMate: elements, relationships and viewpoints
Architecture principles, building blocks and the architecture repository

units.title: Application and data architecture
topics: Application portfolio analysis: the TIME model, rationalisation and dependency maps
Layered, hexagonal and modular-monolith styles; coupling and cohesion
Data architecture: master data, reference data, ownership and stewardship
Canonical data models, data dictionaries and cross-system data flows
The enterprise systems landscape: ERP, CRM, HR and finance and each system of record
Single source of truth and data quality at integration points

units.title: Integration fundamentals and APIs
topics: Integration styles: file transfer, shared database, remote procedure call and messaging
Point-to-point versus hub-and-spoke versus bus; integration debt
REST API design: resources, verbs, status codes, pagination and versioning
OpenAPI specifications; API gateways, rate limiting, OAuth 2.0 and API keys
SOAP and WSDL, GraphQL and gRPC compared
Data formats and transformation: JSON, XML, CSV and schema mapping

units.title: Messaging and event-driven integration
topics: Message queues, publish-subscribe, brokers and topics
Enterprise integration patterns: message router, translator, splitter, aggregator and content-based router
Delivery guarantees: at-most-once, at-least-once, exactly-once; idempotent consumers
Event-driven architecture, event sourcing and CQRS
Dead-letter queues, retries, back-pressure and message ordering
Middleware: enterprise service bus, integration platforms as a service; orchestration versus choreography

units.title: Service-oriented and microservice architectures
topics: SOA principles and the service contract
Microservices: bounded contexts, service boundaries and database per service
Distributed transactions: two-phase commit, the saga pattern and eventual consistency
Service discovery, API composition and the backend-for-frontend pattern
Resilience: timeouts, retries, circuit breakers and bulkheads
When not to use microservices: monolith-first and modular approaches

units.title: Legacy modernisation and migration
topics: Assessing legacy systems: technical debt, risk and business value
Strangler fig pattern and anti-corruption layers
Wrapping mainframe and older systems with APIs; adapters versus screen scraping
Data migration: extract, transform and load, reconciliation, parallel running and cut-over
Replace, rehost, refactor or retire decision matrix

units.title: Interoperability in national and sector platforms
topics: Interoperability levels: technical, semantic, organisational and legal
Government data exchange layers and national digital identity integration
Payment switches and mobile money interoperability: message flows and settlement
Health and agriculture data exchange: HL7 FHIR resources and open data APIs
Security in integration: mutual TLS, token exchange and audit trails

units.title: Architecture governance and roadmaps
topics: Governance bodies: architecture review board, compliance reviews and dispensations
Gap analysis, baseline and target architecture, and transition architectures
Roadmaps, investment prioritisation, business cases and benefit tracking
Architecture metrics: reuse, number of interfaces, technical debt and time to change
Capstone: an architecture deliverable for a merger or digital-government scenario

schedule.title: Enterprise architecture and its frameworks
schedule.exercise: Build a business capability map and a four-layer view of a regional bank, and list the architecture principles that would guide its change.

tasks.title: Place twelve given elements of a regional hospital group into business, application, data and technology layers on a layered diagram
Model a loan approval process across layers in the diagram studio using ArchiMate-style elements and write one viewpoint for the executive sponsor
Work a case in which a firm adopts a framework, choosing which phases to tailor and justifying each choice against stakeholder concerns

schedule.title: Portfolios, styles and ownership
schedule.exercise: Analyse a portfolio of 15 applications with the TIME model and recommend tolerate, invest, migrate or eliminate for each.

tasks.title: Plot twelve applications on a business value versus technical fit grid and assign each a TIME category
Redraw a given tangled monolith as a layered design and a hexagonal design and list the coupling removed by each
Identify duplicate customer records across three given source tables, define the master record rules and write queries that build the golden record

schedule.title: Canonical models, landscapes and data quality
schedule.exercise: Define a canonical customer and order model and map three systems onto it, recording data quality rules at each integration point.

tasks.title: Draw the system landscape of a retailer and mark which system is the system of record for customers, stock and invoices
Design a canonical order schema and write SQL views that present data from two differently shaped source tables in that one form
Write data quality checks for completeness, validity and uniqueness over a merged customer table and report the defect rate per source system

schedule.title: Integration styles and REST APIs
schedule.exercise: Replace six point-to-point links in a given diagram with a hub design and design the REST API for one of the services.

tasks.title: Call a given REST API with GET and POST requests, inspect status codes and headers, and record the response for each case
Count the interfaces in a point-to-point estate of eight systems, redraw it with a hub and compare the number of connections and failure points
Implement a small orders REST service with pagination and versioned routes and write tests that cover error paths and idempotent updates

schedule.title: API contracts, gateways and data formats
schedule.exercise: Write an OpenAPI contract for a payments API, specify gateway policies, and compare REST, GraphQL and gRPC for one use case.

tasks.title: Convert a sample record between JSON, XML and CSV in a script and check that no field is lost or changed
Write an OpenAPI description for three endpoints and implement a gateway wrapper that enforces an API key and a rate limit of ten requests a minute
Choose among REST, GraphQL and gRPC for four integration scenarios in a branching case, scored on payload size, client variety and tooling cost

schedule.title: Queues, publish-subscribe and integration patterns
schedule.exercise: Design a message flow for an order system with splitter, router and aggregator steps and state the delivery guarantee required on each hop.

tasks.title: Step through a producer, queue and two consumers and record how messages are distributed, acknowledged and redelivered
Model an order-handling flow with a content-based router, a splitter and an aggregator, and trace three sample messages through it
Implement an idempotent consumer using message ids, then simulate duplicate deliveries and show that account balances stay correct

schedule.title: Event-driven design and middleware
schedule.exercise: Compare orchestration and choreography for a loan application workflow and write a failure-handling plan for the event flow.

tasks.title: Observe a consumer that keeps failing a message and show it moving to a dead-letter queue after a set number of retries
Build an event-sourced account where the balance is rebuilt by replaying events, and add a read model for statements
Model one business process once as central orchestration and once as choreography, then compare coupling, observability and failure handling

schedule.title: Service-oriented design and microservice boundaries
schedule.exercise: Split a monolithic hospital system into bounded contexts and design a saga for admitting a patient and billing the insurer.

tasks.title: Write the service contract for a stock-check service, listing operations, message formats, error cases and service levels
Identify bounded contexts in a given domain description and draw services with their own databases and the events they publish
Step through a saga with a failing payment step and design the compensating actions that return the order system to a consistent state

schedule.title: Composition and resilience
schedule.exercise: Add timeouts, retries and a circuit breaker to a service-call design, and write a one-page argument for or against microservices for a small firm.

tasks.title: Watch a circuit breaker open, half-open and close as a failing dependency recovers and note the state at each request
Build an API composition endpoint that calls two services in parallel, applies timeouts and returns a partial result when one fails
Decide among a monolith, a modular monolith and microservices for three organisations in a case, justified against team size and change rate

schedule.title: Modernising legacy systems
schedule.exercise: Plan the staged replacement of a legacy payroll system using a strangler approach, including the data migration and cut-over steps.

tasks.title: Score six legacy systems on business value, risk and cost and place each in the replace, rehost, refactor or retire matrix
Draw a strangler migration in three stages with a routing layer and an anti-corruption layer between old and new systems
Migrate records from a legacy schema to a new schema with transform queries and prove completeness with reconciliation counts and checksums

schedule.title: Interoperability and national platforms
schedule.exercise: Trace a mobile money transfer between two providers through a payment switch, naming each message, and propose secure exchange controls.

tasks.title: Draw the message sequence for a cross-network mobile money transfer through a switch, labelling request, response and settlement steps
Retrieve and validate a sample FHIR patient resource from a test server and map three of its fields to a local record format
Resolve a security review case on a government data exchange, selecting authentication, token and audit controls scored against a rubric

schedule.title: Governance, gaps and roadmaps
schedule.exercise: Write a gap analysis from baseline to target architecture for a district assembly and a three-stage roadmap ranked by value and risk.

tasks.title: List the gaps between a given baseline and target architecture and map each gap to a work package on a diagram
Build a roadmap in the diagram studio with dependencies between projects and an ordering justified by value, cost and risk
Chair a simulated review board in a case, approving, conditioning or rejecting four project proposals and scored on principle compliance

schedule.title: Metrics and capstone
schedule.exercise: Produce and defend the capstone architecture pack for a merger of two microfinance firms: current state, target state, integration design and roadmap.

tasks.title: Compute reuse rate, interface count and time to change for a given architecture and compare them against stated targets
Produce a layered target architecture with the main integration interfaces for the merger scenario and annotate each with its pattern
Deploy a reference implementation of the key integration in the cloud console, measure its throughput and failure behaviour, and report the evidence for the review
